title: The Fourier transform is perverse t-exact on the line
statement:
Use the finite-field and adic $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ conventions of [rem-dl-a1-conventions, def-weil-pbc-qbar-category]. Fix a nontrivial additive character $\psi:k_0\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell^\times$ [def-fd-additive-character]. Write $A_0=\mathbf A^1_{k_0}$, $A=A_0\times_{k_0}k$, and use primes for the dual lines. Let $\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ be the transform of [def-fd-transform], with shift $[1]$ and the adic operations of [def-fourier-set].

For Weil complexes [def-weil-weil-sheaf-complex], the classes ${}^pD^{\le0}(A_0)$ and ${}^pD^{\ge0}(A_0)$ mean those fixed pairs whose underlying geometric complexes belong to the perverse classes of [def-per-perverse-subcategories, thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart] on $A$. Write $\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)$ for the category of fixed pairs in that geometric perverse heart, and similarly for $A'_0$. This is the abelian Weil heart in [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart]; a triangulated structure on the category of fixed pairs is not asserted.

Then the Fourier transform is t-exact in the sense of preserving these two classes:
$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi({}^pD^{\le0}(A_0))\subseteq{}^pD^{\le0}(A'_0),\qquad
\operatorname{FT}_\psi({}^pD^{\ge0}(A_0))\subseteq{}^pD^{\ge0}(A'_0).
$$
The same holds for $\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}$ from $A'_0$ to $A_0$. In particular both carry perverse Weil sheaves to perverse Weil sheaves, sharpening the amplitude bound $[-1,1]$ of [thm-fd-fourier-perverse] to amplitude $0$. With the Tate twist of [def-wf-tate-twist],
$$
\operatorname{FT}_\psi:\mathrm{Perv}(A_0)\rightleftarrows\mathrm{Perv}(A'_0):
G=\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(-)(1)
$$
are mutually quasi-inverse exact equivalences of abelian categories.

proof.text: Work throughout on the underlying geometric derived categories and retain the Frobenius isomorphisms. The theorem [thm-fd-transform-well-defined] makes the transform an exact triangulated functor on the underlying bounded constructible categories. Its pullback, rank-one kernel tensor product and compact-support image carry Weil structures, with equivariant composition and exchange maps, by [lem-fix-weil-operations]. At $\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ choose a common finite coefficient field containing the character values for each finite diagram and use the exact scalar-extension compatibility in [prop-functor-package]. This is the adic interpretation of [def-fourier-set], not discrete non-torsion étale sheaves.

The curve description [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart] gives the upper criterion $\mathcal H^aK=0$ for $a>0$, with $\mathcal H^0K$ punctual. It also gives the lower criterion $\mathcal H^aK=0$ for $a<-1$, with no nonzero punctual subsheaf of $\mathcal H^{-1}K$. Standard truncations and cohomology are those of [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology], whose standard structure is preserved by scheme isomorphisms. Geometric Frobenius and its inverse are scheme isomorphisms; their pullbacks reindex the geometric fibres, hence preserve finite support. Applying that exact sheaf equivalence and its inverse to subsheaf inclusions preserves the condition of having no punctual subsheaf. Hence Frobenius is t-exact for both the standard and the perverse structures. Apply [lem-a1-fixed-pair-truncation-orthogonality] to both structures: ordinary truncations are Weil pairs and the perverse lower class is the right orthogonal, in morphisms of Weil pairs, of the shifted upper class.

source.place: Steps 0 and 3: curve descriptions and Frobenius-qualified orthogonality

proof.text: The upper class is stable under $[n]$ for $n\ge0$: ordinary degrees decrease, and for $n>0$ the degree-zero sheaf vanishes. It is extension-closed by the long exact cohomology sequence, since a subquotient of a sheaf supported on a finite union of finite sets has finite support; this long exact sequence is supplied by [lem-weil-heart-short-exact-triangles] for the standard t-structure. Tensor with a Tate line is exact and invertible: the rank-one local freeness of [lem-pur-twist-sheaf-locally-free], the twist construction [def-wf-tate-twist], and inverse evaluation of a rank-one free module give this locally, hence globally. It preserves supports; applying its inverse to any subsheaf inclusion also shows that it preserves the absence of punctual subsheaves. Thus $(1)$ and $(-1)$ preserve both perverse classes by the two curve criteria.

source.place: Step 0: shifts, extensions and Tate lines

proof.text: Let $\mathcal G$ be a punctual Weil sheaf. Its underlying support is a finite Frobenius-stable set, hence is contained in a reduced finite subscheme $Z_0\subset A_0$. By the closed-support assertion of [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology], $\mathcal G=i_*i^*\mathcal G$. Tensoring with $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}$ preserves this support. Compact-support composition and the proper comparison $Ri_!=Ri_*$ of [prop-functor-package] identify its cohomology on $A$ with that on $Z$. After a finite constant-field extension making $a\in k$ rational, [lem-a1-finite-boundary-cohomology] concentrates that cohomology in degree zero. The stalk formula [lem-fd-stalk-formula], at rank one, therefore concentrates every closed geometric fibre of $\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal G)$ in degree $-1$. The exact conservative closed geometric fibres of [lem-dl-a1-constructible-fibres-exact] show that its cohomology sheaves in degrees $\ge0$ vanish. It satisfies the upper criterion.

Now let $\mathcal G$ be any constructible Weil sheaf on $A_0$. For $a\in k$ the stalk formula [lem-fd-stalk-formula] gives
$$\mathcal H^j(\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal G[1]))_a=H_c^{j+2}(A,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}).$$
All data including $a$ and this Artin–Schreier sheaf descend to some finite constant-field extension of $k_0$. Here one uses the same prime-field character underlying $\psi$; no trace from the algebraic closure is used. Apply [lem-zl-affine-curve-range] over that finite field to the twisted constructible Weil sheaf. The displayed group vanishes unless $-2\le j\le0$. Exactness and conservativity of geometric coefficient fibres [lem-dl-a1-constructible-fibres-exact] give $\mathcal H^j=0$ for $j>0$. Only finite support of the degree-zero sheaf remains.

source.place: Step 1(a): degree bound from curve cohomology

proof.text:
Choose a dense open $U\subset A$ on which $\mathcal G$ is lisse, with finite complement, using [sk-lem-coefficient-heart]. It can be chosen over $k_0$: each of the finitely many missing geometric points has finite Frobenius orbit, so remove their entire orbits. Write $j:U\hookrightarrow A$ and $i:Z\hookrightarrow A$. Apply the open–closed triangle [prop-sf-open-closed-triangle-all-stages] to $\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}$. By [prop-functor-package], applying compact cohomology identifies its outer terms with compact cohomology on $U$ and $Z$. The finite-boundary vanishing [lem-a1-finite-boundary-cohomology] gives
$$H_c^2(A,\mathcal G\otimes\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)})\cong H_c^2(U,\mathcal G|_U\otimes\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}|_U).$$
After the same finite constant-field extension as above, $U_0$ is smooth geometrically connected affine, and the twisted restriction is lisse Weil. Thus [lem-a1-affine-hc2] identifies the last group with $(V\otimes\chi_a)_{\pi_1(U)}(-1)$, where $V=\mathcal G_{\bar\eta}$ and $\chi_a$ is the character of $\mathcal L_{\psi(ax)}|_U$. The tensor interpretation of [cor-galois-lisse-representations] identifies this representation with the generic fibre of the twisted sheaf.

source.place: Step 1(a): localization and top cohomology coinvariants

proof.text: The coinvariants $(V\otimes\chi_a)_{\pi_1(U)}$ are nonzero exactly when $V$ has a quotient $\chi_a^{-1}$: a nonzero functional on the coinvariant vector space is a nonzero invariant functional on $V\otimes\chi_a$, and tensoring by the inverse line converts it into an equivariant map $V\to\chi_a^{-1}$. Conversely such a nonzero map is onto the one-dimensional target and factors through the coinvariants after tensoring. This is finite-dimensional vector-space duality, with no semisimplicity hypothesis.

These characters are pairwise distinct. By the tensor and inverse identities of [lem-fd-as-characters], equality $\chi_a=\chi_b$ would make $\mathcal L_{\psi((a-b)x)}|_U$ trivial, using the tensor equivalence [cor-galois-lisse-representations]. The line $A$ is connected and normal (smooth-curve normality [lem-sc-smooth-normal]), so the dense-open fundamental-group surjection of [lem-wf-dense-open-pi1-surjective] makes this rank-one representation trivial on $A$ itself. If $a\ne b$, the nontrivial prime-field Artin–Schreier cohomology computation [lem-fd-cohomology-affine-line-character] instead gives $H^0(A,\mathcal L_{\psi((a-b)x)})=0$. A trivial rank-one sheaf has a nonzero constant section, a contradiction. Also [lem-fd-as-characters] identifies $\chi_a^{-1}=\chi_{-a}$.

source.place: Step 1(a): distinctness on the dense open

proof.text: At most $r=\dim V$ distinct characters can be quotients of $V$. Indeed choose a nonzero quotient functional $f_i:V\to\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$ for each distinct quotient character $\lambda_i$. They satisfy $f_i\rho(g)=\lambda_i(g)f_i$. If they had a nonzero linear relation of minimal length, its length would be at least two. Choose two indices $i,j$ in it and $g$ with $\lambda_i(g)\ne\lambda_j(g)$. Precompose the relation by $\rho(g)$ and subtract $\lambda_j(g)$ times the original relation. This is a shorter nonzero relation, a contradiction. The functionals are independent, so their number is at most $r$. This includes $V=0$, when no quotient exists.

source.place: Step 1(a): elementary rank bound for distinct quotient characters

proof.text: It follows that $\mathcal H^0\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal G[1])$ has nonzero closed geometric fibres at at most $r$ points $a\in k$. The finite lisse stratification and locally constant ranks in [lem-per-adic-heart-pullback-fibres] rule out a nonzero generic fibre: the stratum containing the generic point contains a dense open, which over the infinite field $k$ has infinitely many closed points. All remaining nonzero fibres are among the finite exceptional set. Hence the degree-zero sheaf is punctual. Together with the degree bound in step 5 and [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart], this proves that $\operatorname{FT}_\psi(\mathcal G[1])$ belongs to the upper class.

source.place: Step 1(a): finite support from the rank bound

proof.text: Let $K$ be an upper-class Weil complex. Its bounded ordinary truncation tower, available equivariantly by [lem-a1-fixed-pair-truncation-orthogonality] and [lem-a1-qbar-open-closed-cohomology], has factors $\mathcal H^0K$ and $\mathcal H^{-m}K[m]$ for finitely many $m\ge1$. The first factor is punctual; each other factor is $(\mathcal H^{-m}K[1])[m-1]$. Steps 3–10 put their Fourier images in the upper class. Induct up this finite tower, starting with its zero truncation; the transform sends each underlying truncation triangle to a distinguished triangle, and upper extension-closure puts the middle image in the upper class at each stage. Thus $\operatorname{FT}_\psi$ preserves the upper class. The argument applies to every nontrivial character, in particular $\psi^{-1}$ with the two lines exchanged. Tate-line stability from step 3 then gives upper preservation by $G=\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(-)(1)$ too.

source.place: Step 1: finite ordinary truncation induction and inverse character

proof.text: Fourier inversion [lem-fd-inversion] at rank one gives natural isomorphisms $\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}\operatorname{FT}_\psi(K)\cong K(-1)$ and, applied to $\psi^{-1}$, $\operatorname{FT}_\psi\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}(M)\cong M(-1)$. By [prop-base-linear] the transform commutes with $(1)$, and the isomorphism is one of Weil complexes. Tensoring with the inverse Tate line cancels the $(-1)$ twist, as in step 3. Hence $G\operatorname{FT}_\psi\cong\mathrm{id}$ and $\operatorname{FT}_\psi G\cong\mathrm{id}$ as functors on Weil pairs. These two natural isomorphisms exhibit mutually inverse equivalences; a triangulated structure on pairs is not needed.

Let $K$ lie in the lower class on $A_0$, and let $M$ be an upper-class Weil pair shifted into ${}^pD^{\le-1}(A'_0)$. The equivalence in step 12 gives
$$\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm W}(M,\operatorname{FT}_\psi K)\cong\operatorname{Hom}_{\mathrm W}(GM,K).$$
The shift comparison for the underlying Fourier functor is equivariant by its Weil operations. Step 11 therefore puts $GM=G(M[-1])[1]$ in ${}^pD^{\le-1}(A_0)$. The right-hand side vanishes by the fixed-pair orthogonality of [lem-a1-fixed-pair-truncation-orthogonality] applied in step 2. Its converse puts $\operatorname{FT}_\psi K$ in the lower class. Apply this argument with $\psi^{-1}$ and the two lines exchanged to obtain lower preservation for $\operatorname{FT}_{\psi^{-1}}$. Step 3 gives lower preservation for $G$ as well.

source.place: Step 3: transport of orthogonality in the fixed-pair Hom groups

proof.text: Upper and lower preservation restrict the two functors to the Weil perverse hearts of [thm-a1-curve-perverse-heart], and the natural isomorphisms of step 12 restrict with them. Thus they are mutually inverse equivalences of the stated abelian categories. An additive equivalence preserves a kernel: applying its inverse identifies maps killed by the image morphism with maps killed by the original morphism, so the original kernel's universal factorization gives the image kernel's unique factorization. The same argument applies to cokernels. Both Fourier functors are additive by their underlying triangulated construction, so their equivalences on the hearts are exact. This proves the last assertion without treating Weil pairs as a triangulated category.

source.place: Step 4: exact equivalence on the hearts
